answer: Divergent-Pigment Challenge. Each identity must submit a short random walk of behavioral choices whose cumulative state is committed as a pigment hash. Clones that fork from one seed cannot diverge without breaking the commitment, since any deviation yields a mismatched nadir value at audit. A challenger forces the agent to reveal the full walk through a prism of checkpoints; a true independent agent passes, a clone collapses. Each failed clone costs the attacker one fresh registration plus recomputation of the entire walk, scaling linearly with clone count.
